title: Request-shape cost tiling & SKU recommendations (working spreadsheet)
content:
Goal: build a simple, actionable mapping from observed request shapes -> recommended SKU tiling + model family fallsbacks + region multipliers to improve per-token margin without degrading p99 latency.

Context / motivation:
- Many customers have bimodal request shapes (short prompts, long completions). Current flat SKU tiling wastes capacity: short-only workloads underutilize slots, long-only workloads overconsume memory.
- Regional COGS vary: EU power+egress ~1.15x US-west; APAC GPU lease premiums ~1.3x. Need per-region multiplier baked into pricing guidance.

Key definitions (working):
- request_shape: distribution vector of {prompt_len, completion_len, tokens_per_request}.
- slot_tile: number of concurrent requests mapped to a slot type (latency tier).
- SKU_tiering: mapping of model_family + quantization profile -> GPU SKU candidate.

Quick model of per-token COGS (single-region):
- base_gpu_hour_cost = amortized GPU + host + license + infra (~$2.8/hr for A100 equiv on reserved)
- effective_tokens_per_hour = (tokens_per_request * requests_per_sec) * 3600 * batching_efficiency
- per_token_cogs = base_gpu_hour_cost / effective_tokens_per_hour + egress_per_token + storage_p99_amortized

Example rows (simulated):
- Shape A: prompt 20, completion 40, 40 rps, batching_eff 2.1 -> tokens/hr ~ 40*(60)*3600*2.1 = (we keep calc simplified in sheet) -> per-token cogs = $0.0012
- Shape B: prompt 5, completion 10, 120 rps, batching_eff 1.05 -> per-token cogs = $0.0026 (short unbatchable)
- Shape C: prompt 80, completion 600, 2 rps, kv-cache reuse -> per-token cogs = $0.0009 (long but steady)

SKU tiling recommendations (heuristic phases):
1) Observe: compute 90th percentile tokens/request and request concurrency patterns by route.
2) Bucket routes into 3 shapes: burst-short, long-stream, mixed.
3) Assign default tiling:
   - burst-short -> high-concurrency small-slot (tile 128x infer cores), prefer quantized fp8/4x to reduce cost; prioritize small-seq optimized kernels.
   - long-stream -> large-memory tiles (dedicated KV cache), fewer concurrent slots per GPU, prefer fp16 for stability at high seq lengths.
   - mixed -> hybrid routing: short requests get low-latency pool; long requests go to throughput pool with batching windows.
4) Region multipliers: US-west (1.0), US-east (1.03), EU (1.15), APAC (1.30). These should be adjustable per account.

Tradeoffs and checks:
- Latency SLO: any SKU change must include a p99 increase check in the canary (metric: p99 tokens/second and tail-kernel CPU wait).
- Quality: quantization fallback thresholds: if eval drop > 0.6% on redwood-eval set, block fp4 fallback.
- Ops complexity: each additional tiling increases routing complexity + observability costs; recommend max 4 tilings per region initially.

Prioritization matrix (playbook):
- High value & high variance routes -> immediate tiling + A/B with 5% traffic.
- Low value, low variance -> default pool (no change).
- High value, long-tail requests -> consider prefetch/kv-cache optimization before tiling.

Sample action items (owners + timeline):
- (Avery) Build per-route request_shape exporter into console (2 sprints).
- (Marcus) Add region multiplier config to pricing sim (1 sprint).
- (Leila) Run 10-customer pilot of tiling rules (4 weeks).
- (Diego) Add eval regression gate for quantized fallbacks in CI (3 weeks).

Open questions / hypotheses to validate:
- Hypothesis 1: tiling based on tokens/request reduces per-token COGS by >12% for top 20% variable routes.
- Hypothesis 2: region-specific SKU mixes (cheaper GPU family in EU) can preserve latency SLO if paired with local caching.
- Measurement plan: A/B test with matched baseline for p50/p90/p99 latency, per-token cost, and quality (eval on golden prompts).

Appendix (scratch calculations & example formulas for the sheet):
- tokens_per_hour = requests_per_sec * avg_tokens_per_request * 3600 * batching_factor
- per_token_cogs = (gpu_hour_cost / tokens_per_hour) + (egress_cost_per_token) + (amortized_storage_per_token)
- margin_estimate = (list_price_per_token - per_token_cogs) / list_price_per_token

Notes: this is intentionally informal — spreadsheet tab layout recommended:
- tab 1: observed request_shape samples (raw)
- tab 2: regional ratecard + multiplier inputs
- tab 3: SKU tiling simulation grid (slot sizes x concurrency x batching_eff)
- tab 4: recommendations + rollout checklist

If folks prefer I can convert to a fully formula’d google-sheet with scenario toggles and a simple slider UI for region multipliers and tiling granularity. For now keeping as a compact working sheet for discussion.

Last quick thought: avoid adding too many model-family specific hedges early. Start with three families: "latency-optimized", "throughput-optimized", "large-memory" and expand once we see customer delta.
